title: Conditionals & The Apodosis Connector (Fa-)
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 35; Ryding Ch. 39 §§39.1–39.3)
objectives: Distinguish real/possible conditions (إِنْ, إِذَا) from contrary-to-fact conditions (لَوْ, لَوْلَا).
Apply jussive governance in both protasis (sharṭ) and apodosis (jazāʾ) with إِنْ.
Apply fāʾ al-jazāʾ (فَـ) before non-verbal, imperative, negated, or particle-introduced result clauses.
recallPrompt: From Chapter 16: What happens to sound, afʿāl al-khamsah, and defective verbs in the jussive mood?

sections.heading: Protasis (Al-Sharṭ) & Apodosis (Al-Jazāʾ)
sections.body: Classical Arabic conditional sentences consist of a conditional particle, a condition clause (al-sharṭ), and a result clause (al-jazāʾ). Real or possible conditions use إِنْ ('if' — governing two jussives or two past verbs) and إِذَا ('when/if' — typically taking a past verb with present/future meaning). Hypothetical/counterfactual conditions use لَوْ ('if [it were/had been]') with past verbs and لَـ on the result.

sections.label: Mandatory Fāʾ al-Jazāʾ Environments
sections.summary: The result clause MUST be introduced by فَـ (fāʾ al-jazāʾ) whenever the result is: (1) a nominal sentence, (2) an imperative or prohibition, (3) negated by لَنْ or مَا, or (4) introduced by قَدْ, سَـ, or سَوْفَ.

sections.heading: Conditional Particles & Structures
rows: If you strive, you will succeed.
If he asks you, then answer him.
Had he studied, he would have succeeded.

sections.translation: If you are patient, then God is with you.
sections.irab: إِنْ: حَرْفُ شَرْطٍ جَازِمٌ | تَصْبِرُوا: فِعْلُ الشَّرْطِ مَجْزُومٌ بِحَذْفِ النُّونِ | فَاللَّهُ مَعَكُمْ: جُمْلَةٌ اسْمِيَّةٌ فِي مَحَلِّ جَزْمٍ جَوَابُ الشَّرْطِ
sections.notes: Because the result clause (اللَّهُ مَعَكُمْ) is a nominal sentence, fāʾ al-jazāʾ (فَـ) is obligatory.

sections.heading: Conditional Pronouns
sections.body: مَنْ ('whoever'), مَا ('whatever'), and مَتَى ('whenever') also govern two jussives just like إِنْ (e.g., مَنْ يَزْرَعْ يَحْصُدْ 'Whoever sows, reaps').
